office_does: A King County Northeast Electoral District District Court judge hears and decides misdemeanor criminal cases, small claims, traffic cases and protection orders for a four-year term; in practice the discretion is in pretrial release, sentencing, protection orders and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: An open seat (Judge Marcus Naylor is reported to be retiring). Jan Trasen, a public defender for 26 years and now a full-time administrative law judge, finished first in the August primary with 47.5% against Bianca Tse, a former King County prosecutor for 16 years who sits pro tem in this court (27.9%). KCBA rates Trasen Exceptionally Well Qualified and Tse Qualified.

candidates.summary: Administrative law judge and King County District Court pro tem, after 26 years as a public defender and appellate attorney. She finished first in the primary and holds Exceptionally Well Qualified ratings from KCBA, WWL and JAJEC.
highlights: Full-time administrative law judge (Child & Family Care Division) and judge pro tem in this court [S1][S5]
26 years of public defense and appellate work, 16 at the Washington Appellate Project [S1][S5]
Lists mental-health and substance-use treatment options to reduce recidivism among her priorities [S4]
Rated Exceptionally Well Qualified by KCBA, Washington Women Lawyers and JAJEC [S8][S9][S11]
First in the August primary with 59,661 votes (47.5%) [S7]

judicial.basis: Treatment-to-reduce-recidivism plank is the only reform-leaning signal; no interpretive-method statement. Evidence unchanged since the primary, where refutation set this to low.

safety.basis: 26-year public-defense and appellate formation plus a stated priority on mental-health and substance-use treatment to reduce recidivism; evidence unchanged since the primary, re-verified on her site.

experience.basis: Runs on a record case: full-time ALJ, pro tem in this court, KCBA Exceptionally Well Qualified rating and a long judicial endorsement list.

candidates.summary: Bellevue attorney and King County District Court pro tem since 2021 who spent 16 years as a King County deputy prosecutor, then ran a bilingual private civil practice. She leads in fundraising.
highlights: 16 years as a King County deputy prosecutor, trying cases up to homicide [S4][S6]
Judge pro tem in this court and Eastside municipal courts since 2021 [S2][S4]
Says the job "requires different skills than being an administrative law judge" and that politics should play no role in courts [S1]
Rated Qualified by KCBA and Washington Women Lawyers and Exceptionally Well Qualified by JAJEC [S8][S9][S11]
Second in the August primary with 27.9%; has raised about $60,400 [S7][S12]

safety.basis: 16-year prosecution formation including homicide trials; no bail or diversion positions documented. Evidence unchanged since the primary.

experience.basis: Runs on readiness: a stated 30-year trial-court career and five years pro tem in this court.
